controls.requirement: Each agent system MUST implement one bounded workflow with a named accepted outcome and accountable owners.
Deterministic rules, policy enforcement, state transitions, and privileged effects MUST execute outside model generation.
Multi-agent decomposition SHOULD require distinct context, permission, latency, or specialization boundaries.
Every decision-bearing source MUST declare an owner, source-of-truth status, classification, revision, and freshness objective.
Retrieved, user-supplied, tool-returned, and external content MUST remain data and MUST NOT acquire instruction authority.
Adaptive retrieval SHOULD use an explicit evidence-sufficiency check and a bounded query-rewrite budget.
Persisted memory and shared conclusions MUST retain provenance, trust labels, validation state, and invalidation rules.
Every model-visible tool MUST have a narrow typed contract, explicit owner, effect class, and failure taxonomy.
Large capability catalogs SHOULD expose progressive search, describe, and execute interfaces instead of loading all tools.
Read, stage, commit, administrative, and destructive operations MUST use distinct tools and authorization policies.
Tool output MUST include structured status and typed errors; natural-language success claims MUST NOT prove completion.
Every run MUST use a dedicated workload identity distinct from the initiating user and target service identity.
Delegated actions MUST intersect agent capability with the initiating caller's current authorization and tenant scope.
Authorization MUST be evaluated at the action boundary and MUST fail closed on missing or stale policy context.
Secrets MUST remain behind a trusted broker and MUST NOT enter model context, tool output, logs, or sandbox storage.
Runtime network egress MUST be denied by default and constrained by destination, protocol, method, and agent identity.
Model-generated code and general-purpose execution MUST run in an isolated environment with bounded CPU, memory, time, filesystem, and network.
Each high-severity threat MUST map to preventive, detective, recovery, and executable negative-test controls.
Tenant identifiers MUST bind authorization, retrieval, caches, durable state, encryption context, and tool requests.
Every side-effecting operation MUST use service-enforced idempotency keyed to the stable business operation.
Loops MUST bound steps, elapsed time, retries, tool calls, model cost, and parallel workers with explicit terminal reasons.
Consequential effects MUST be followed by source-of-truth readback that verifies the declared business postcondition.
Parallel work MUST define fan-out, capacity, cancellation, idempotency, merge, conflict, and partial-failure semantics.
Workflow state MUST be explicit, versioned, replayable, and independent from model context and transport sessions.
State MUST be committed only after its validation, authorization, and approval gate succeeds.
Each state class MUST declare storage boundary, classification, retention, recovery point, and deletion behavior.
Release evaluation MUST cover contracts, components, trajectories, artifacts, external effects, safety, and operating budgets.
Evaluation fixtures, graders, tests, and pass signals MUST be isolated from agent-controlled code and write paths.
High-risk slices and prohibited effects MUST have separate thresholds that aggregate performance cannot offset.
Each production incident and diagnosed behavior cluster MUST produce a replayable regression case before closure.
Semantic judges SHOULD be calibrated against expert labels with agreement, drift, and slice-level error tracking.
Approval interfaces MUST expose proposed effect, evidence, uncertainty, policy decision, postcondition, and available alternatives.
Humans MUST be able to pause, reject, edit, escalate, and resume work without losing trace or state integrity.
Each run MUST emit versioned trace data for identity, context, tools, policy, approvals, state, effects, readback, cost, and stop reason.
Production systems MUST provide kill switches for new work, writes, identities, egress, and individual capability bundles.
Each severe failure mode MUST have a detection query, containment step, readback, recovery procedure, owner, and regression link.
Service objectives MUST include accepted outcomes, prohibited effects, duplicate effects, cycle time, cost, and recovery success.
Durable workflows SHOULD support checkpoints, replay, version migration, cancellation propagation, and dead-letter recovery.
Cost MUST be attributed per accepted outcome across model, tool, compute, storage, wait, retry, and human-review components.
Every run MUST enforce cost and resource budgets with a terminal budget-exhausted state and escalation policy.
